test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement.

**Statement:**

The book ‘P’ emphasizes only on population of India and its related problems during 2001-2015.

**Conclusions:**

I. Increasing population is the biggest problem in India.

II. The book 'P' is the only book which deals with the problem of population in India.

options.text: Both I and II conclusion follow
Neither I nor II conclusion follows

solution:
The logic followed here is:

Given statements:

The book ‘P’ emphasizes only on population of India and its related problems during 2001-2015 → The statement is talking about the book 'P' which emphasizes only on population of India and its related problems during 2001-2015.

**Conclusions:**

I. Increasing population is the biggest problem in India → Not Follows (as from the given statement we can say that population is one of the problems in India but **we can not conclude that is the biggest problem in India**).

II. The book 'P' is the only book which deals with the problem of population in India → Not Follows (as from the given statement we can say that book 'P' is one among the books that emphasizes on the population of India and **not the only book to do so**). 

Hence, **neither I nor II conclusion follows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**If definitive words like all, always, at least, only, exactly, and so on are used, then such words make the conclusion invalid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• If there are two or more sentences that are used to frame a statement, then, the sentences must be interrelated, and mutual contradiction should be there.
 
• Do not look for truthful notions. The information provided in the statement is the only requirement for a student to answer the question. No assumptions must be made.
 
• Read the statement carefully and look for keywords that are common between the statement and the conclusions.
 
• If there is more than one conclusion that is applicable to the statement, students must ensure that the conclusions they opt for have some relation with each other.
